Definition: transitively (in dual) the jaws (as taking food); in transitively, spoil (and captives) (as taken)
BiblicalUsage: malqôwach names both the jaws that take food and the spoil taken in war. In Numbers 31:11 the word stands where Israel takes all the spoil and prey after battle, and in Isaiah 49:24 it asks whether the prey can be taken from the mighty. The same word turns up in the psalmist's suffering in Psalms 22:15, where his tongue cleaves to his jaws. Taking and being taken run through the whole word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe malqôwach shows me that what is taken is never finally lost to God. He promises in Isaiah 49:25 to take the captives of the mighty away, and I hold that His rescue reaches even the prey already carried off. No loss of mine is beyond His taking back.
